correctness.rationale: On an m≥2 unit-edge real metric star with arclength plus w>0 Dirac at exactly one OUTER leaf, nodal Gram G_w=G_0+w e1e1^T is positive definite and Sherman–Morrison gives the stated inverse. At ordinary leaf, the affine kernel has negative common center and positive outer endpoint values, plus positive atom q; exact absolute-linear integral J(a,b)=(a²+b²)/(2(a+b)) yields the rational Λ_m(w). Explicit positive-polynomial differences prove R_ordinary>R_hub and R_atom for all m,w; affine kernel convexity, with strict sign disagreement, excludes all interior normers. Differentiating gives a coefficientwise positive derivative; rank-one limits and the m=2 cubic give the unique crossover. Since P1=1, negative-part mass gives exact positivity defect and witnesses. Independently formed exact rational Gram inverses and absolute kernel integrals in SymPy for m=2,3,4,6 and w=1/10,1,4: all twelve cases match Λ and the proposed norming leaves. Actual verify_leaf_atom.py read and symbolic identities/finitude checked; symbolic algebra plus positivity reasoning establishes universal claims.

originality.rationale: Earlier exact weighted-metric-star spline formula assumes purely diffuse edge measures; a different same-day mixed-measure theorem places a positive atom at the hub and obtains a different norm/threshold and norming leaves. Neither permits relocating the atom to a single OUTER leaf via an isometric symmetry of the star (center has degree m). Oswald concerns Euclidean triangulations and a uniform-bound counterexample, not this atomic graph. The new rank-one perturbation at a leaf, strict increase and movement of worst evaluation to other leaves survive best-of-knowledge with residual specialist literature risk.
